clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the President's Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History, of not more than 11 members appointed from the public and private sectors, with up to two Co-Chairs designated by the President. Terminated by express revocation. Section 3 of Executive Order 13225, signed September 28, 2001, ends its lead-in with "committees that have terminated and whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (c) reads "Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, estab-". Section 5 reads "Sec. 5. This order shall be effective September 30, 2001.", so the end is dated 2001-09-30, the stated effective date. The item continues on the following lines with the words lishing the President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History.

Section 2(a) directs the Commission to make recommendations to the President, through the Co-Chairs, on ways to acknowledge and celebrate the roles and accomplishments of women in American history. Terminated by express revocation. Section 3 of Executive Order 13225, signed September 28, 2001, ends its lead-in with "committees that have terminated and whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (c) reads "Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, estab-". Section 5 reads "Sec. 5. This order shall be effective September 30, 2001.", so the end is dated 2001-09-30, the stated effective date. The item continues on the following lines with the words lishing the President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History.

Section 2(b) directs the Commission to meet to carry out its work. Terminated by express revocation. Section 3 of Executive Order 13225, signed September 28, 2001, ends its lead-in with "committees that have terminated and whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (c) reads "Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, estab-". Section 5 reads "Sec. 5. This order shall be effective September 30, 2001.", so the end is dated 2001-09-30, the stated effective date. The item continues on the following lines with the words lishing the President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History.

Section 2(c) requires a final report with the Commission's recommendations to the President by March 1, 1999. That is a report deadline, not an end. Terminated by express revocation. Section 3 of Executive Order 13225, signed September 28, 2001, ends its lead-in with "committees that have terminated and whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (c) reads "Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, estab-". Section 5 reads "Sec. 5. This order shall be effective September 30, 2001.", so the end is dated 2001-09-30, the stated effective date. The item continues on the following lines with the words lishing the President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History.  Later event: Executive Order 13136, signed 1999-09-03, amends section 2(c) by deleting the date March 1, 1999 and inserting December 31, 2000, in order, in its words, to extend the life of the Commission; a report date, not an end, and the clause continues, amended. Executive Order 13136 also recites that the Commission had already made a report to the President, which shows a report existed before September 3, 1999 but gives no date, and which the order treated as leaving the Commission in existence.

Section 3(a) directs the heads of executive departments and agencies, to the extent permitted by law and where practicable, to give the Co-Chairs the information on women's history that they request. Terminated by express revocation. The item continues on the following lines with the words lishing the President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History.

Section 3(b) provides that members serve without compensation, with travel expenses allowed to private sector members. Terminated by express revocation. Section 3 of Executive Order 13225, signed September 28, 2001, ends its lead-in with "committees that have terminated and whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (c) reads "Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, estab-". Section 5 reads "Sec. 5. This order shall be effective September 30, 2001.", so the end is dated 2001-09-30, the stated effective date. The item continues on the following lines with the words lishing the President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History.

Section 3(c) directs the General Services Administration, subject to appropriations, to provide funding, administrative services, facilities and staff, and has the Administrator of General Services perform the administrative functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act except reporting to the Congress. Terminated by express revocation. Section 3 of Executive Order 13225, signed September 28, 2001, ends its lead-in with "committees that have terminated and whose work is completed, are revoked:"; item (c) reads "Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, estab-". Section 5 reads "Sec. 5. This order shall be effective September 30, 2001.", so the end is dated 2001-09-30, the stated effective date. The item continues on the following lines with the words lishing the President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History.

Section 3(d) provides that the Commission shall terminate 60 days after the submission of its final report. That keys the end to the date of the final report; no held source dates it, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines it is not claimed as the end and is a functionally spent report-relative provision, date not held. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register text of Executive Order 13090 (63 FR 36151, PDF pages 1-2 of the 1998-07-02 issue; sha256 030b83d9...), headed Executive Order 13090 of June 29, 1998, President’s Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History, matching the census register row (1998-06-29). Text and inventory: eight scopes cover sections 1 through 3(d) to the signature; I confirm the inventory. All clauses belong to one advisory commission. Ending: Executive Order 13225 section 3(c) revokes Executive Order 13090, as amended by Executive Order 13136, effective September 30, 2001 (section 5). The report deadline in section 2(c) and the report-relative termination in section 3(d) are not ends (owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines); Executive Order 13136, whose recital shows the Commission still in existence on 1999-09-03, extended the life of the Commission. Original grade: Federal Register machine text.

savings.reason: Executive Order 13225 contains no wording that preserves the order establishing the President's Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History: its continuance sections concern other committees and its revocation section revokes this order without exception. Reports or other work already done are completed acts; nothing continues the body.
